annotations.text:
Three answers to the question FEATURE_SCOPING_BRIEF.md §7 leaves open: how does a superset behave once you are actually training?

All three read supersetGroupId, which templates already write. Tick a checkbox in any of them to feel the difference — that is the whole decision.

B · AUTO-ADVANCE — the brief's recommendation, and the leading candidate.

Ticking a set jumps you to the paired lift. A bracket under the tabs shows the pairing; the un-selected half carries a ring so you can see where the tick sends you. Rest inside the group is a short transition bar with a Go now; full rest only after the last lift.

Tradeoff: SetTableView is untouched, but the screen moves under you — a mis-tap lands you on the wrong lift.

A · GROUPED ROUNDS — the pair collapses into one tab and the set table becomes rounds.

Best match for how people actually think (1a/1b, three rounds), and one rest timer per round rather than per set.

Tradeoff: this is a restructure of the set table, not an addition to it. The 36/74/74/42/44/40 row does not fit two exercise names, so the row had to be redesigned — which is the ~5,300 lines the decision record deferred.

C · MARKED ONLY — the bracket, no rest inside the group, and a prompt. Navigation never changes.

Cheapest by a wide margin and nothing can surprise you mid-set.

Tradeoff: you still walk yourself between tabs, which is the part that makes supersets tedious today. This mostly sells the feature rather than delivering it.

MAKING ONE MID-WORKOUT — needed by all three, and absent today: grouping only exists in the template editor.

The tab strip already has a long-press menu (Move Left/Right, Replace, Delete), so Superset with… has an obvious home and no new surface. Long-press the tab, pick the partner, done.

One thing to fix underneath, whichever wins: SetRepository.create takes no supersetGroupId, so a set added during a live workout is silently ungrouped even on a paired exercise. Grouping is stored per set, not per exercise — so a real session ends up half-tagged the moment anything starts reading the field.
